issues.issue: The representation qualifies itself by reference to what is "described on Schedule 5.8 or in an Offering Circular," but no Offering Circular is attached to or identified in the Agreement. The exception is measured by a document outside the instrument.

The representation that "the Lender's Liens are validly created, perfected, and first priority Liens, subject only to Permitted Liens" is hard to reconcile with the Permitted Liens definition and Section 2.1(b), which contemplate existing Schedule P-1 liens "specifically identified thereon as entitled to have priority over the Lender's Liens." First priority and permitted senior liens cannot both hold.

This representation, captioned "Fraudulent Transfer," rests entirely on the defined term "Solvent," which the Agreement reduces to a bare balance-sheet comparison of assets and debts. The caption and the defined test do not measure the same thing.

The representation is qualified three times by "(taken as a whole)" and then requires that the information not be "incomplete by omitting to state any fact necessary to make such information (taken as a whole) not misleading." Whether a specific false statement is cured by the aggregate is exactly what the qualifier leaves open.

After a detailed schedule of dated deliverables, item (h) requires "such other reports as to the Collateral or the financial condition of each Borrower and its Subsidiaries, as Lender may request" — an open catch-all whose reach against the enumerated items is undefined, and breach of Section 6.2 is an immediate Event of Default under Section 8.2(a).

The collection covenant is circular — "use commercially reasonable efforts ... to promptly and diligently collect and enforce payment of all Notes Receivable to the extent that it is commercially reasonable to do so and in a commercially reasonable manner" — so the standard measures itself. No benchmark for adequate collection effort is supplied.

Borrowers must deliver policies "with an endorsement naming Lender as the sole loss payee (under a satisfactory lender's loss payable endorsement) or additional insured, as appropriate" — the choice between the two, and who decides what is "appropriate," is not stated. The difference matters to who controls proceeds under Section 6.8(b).

The enumerated separateness covenants run "(a) ... (c) ... and (d)" with no clause (b), so one item of the list the parties evidently agreed on is missing from the operative text. Whether an unstated separateness undertaking binds the Borrowers is left unresolved by the face of the section.

The covenant applies only "to the extent necessary to comply with Section 4.2," which requires delivery of enough notes to keep $250,000,000 of Eligible Notes Receivable with Lender, whereas the Eligible Notes Receivable definition, clauses (r) and (s), conditions eligibility of every note on delivery and recorded assignment. The delivery duty is therefore stated at two different scopes.

This covenant requires escrowed amounts to be deposited into "a Deposit Account that is subject to a perfected Lender's Lien," while Section 2.6(e) requires the same funds to be held in an Escrow Account at a Cash Management Bank under a Cash Management Agreement. The two locations for the same money are stated independently.

The covenant requires escrow instructions that call for "delivery by such maker of each of the documents listed in Section 3.3(z)," but Section 3.3 has only subsections (a) through (f) and contains no clause (z); the documents intended are those in Section 3.1(t). The disbursement condition points to a subsection that does not exist.

Section 7.4 bars any disposal of assets other than Permitted Dispositions, while Section 7.3(c) bars only the disposal of "all or any substantial part of its assets" other than Permitted Dispositions. Two overlapping prohibitions of different reach cover the same conduct.
